newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: HOWARD SAYS PROSSER OK TO PASS ON SOME OF PORTFOLIO
The Prime Minister says he has no difficulty with Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser handing part of his portfolio to senior minister John Moore.
Mr Howard has resisted pressure from the Opposition to sack Mr Prosser on the grounds his private business interests conflict with his ministerial responsibilities.

The Opposition has described Mr Prosser as a lame-duck minister because he recently stood aside from one of his portfolio duties, relating to retail tenancies, because of a possible conflict of interest.
Mr Howard has told Sydney Radio 2UE, that there was nothing wrong with that.
"In the past ministers have often thought that they've had a conflict of interest situation on both sides, and you get somebody else to do it." he said.
GOVT REJECTS RACISM MOTIVATED PLAN TO DEPORT US ACTIVIST
The Federal Government has rejected allegations that the decision to deport United States activist Lorenzo Ervin was motivated by racism.
Mr Ervin is in custody in Brisbane after having his visa cancelled by Acting Immigration Minister Amanda Vanstone.
His lawyers are seeking to overturn the Government's decision.
Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith says Mr Ervin was convicted of hijacking a plane in the United States, and alleged not to have disclosed that conviction when he applied for a visa.
Mr Reith has rejected any allegations racism was a motive in the plan to deport Mr Ervin.
Mr Reith said the Government has the responsibility to control people coming into Australia on the basis of whether or not they are of good character.
He says Mr Ervin is "clearly" not of good character, and any allegations of racism are "completely wrong and completely unreasonable."
FATHERS GROUP URGES GOVERNMENT TO FUND APPEAL
A national organisation representing fathers, wants the Federal Goverment to fund a High Court appeal, against a Family Court decision on relocating children from non-custodial parents.
The full bench of the Family Court yesterday dismissed an appeal by a father who wanted to stop his former wife moving from Queensland to Victoria with their children.
Secretary of "Dads Australia" John Clarke, said the law needs to be reformed to allow both parents appropriate access to their children.

"The system needs to be reformed to the extent that if a couple separates, both parents automatically get, without argument, or contest, a guaranteed contact arrangement with their children, that is enforceable properly by the law" Mr Clark said.
He said Attorney General, Darryl Williams should either fund this man's High Court appeal against the decision or initiate the Government's own appeal to test out the legislation properly.
PLANES ON STANDBY FOR EVACUATION OF AUSSIES FROM CAMBODIA
In Malaysia and Darwin, Australian Air Force Hercules transport planes are on stand-by in case they are needed to evacuate Australians from Cambodia.
This follows the outbreak of fighting in and around the capital, Phnom Penh between forces loyal to the nation's first and second Prime Ministers.
Australian foreign minister, Alexander Downer, said he expects to make an announcement later today following the withdrawal of American embassy staff in the Cambodian capital.
The US has announced it is cutting its embassy staff in Phnom Penh from 61 to 20, and advising their family members and all other US citizens to leave Cambodia.
A State Department spokesman said the Pentagon has made contingency plans for a possible military evacuation, but it is hoped the diplomats and others can leave by civilian transport.
Almost 1,000 foreign citizens have already been evacuated from the city.
CALLS FOR SUPER TO HELP HOME BUYERS REJECTED
A peak superannuation body has rejected calls to make super funds available for lower income earners to buy a home.
The Life, Investment and Superannuation Association, or LISA, has written to Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, saying the proposal cannot be justified because of the cost.
Both the Real Estate Institute and the Housing Industry Association have urged the Government to relax superannuation laws to help people who otherwise could not afford a home deposit.
They have said the proposal would benefit all sides.
But LISA's Executive Director John Maroney said the proposal would reduce national savings, increase pension outlays, and cut across efforts to preserve superannuation for retirement.
The Prime Minister said this week the Government's examining the proposal, but there are arguments for and against. - - - -
PAINTING USED IN EVIDENCE IN NATIVE TITLE CLAIM
An Aboriginal traditional owner has produced a painting of Alice Springs, as evidence in a native title claim.
A Federal Court hearing continues today, into a claim for native title on areas of crown land in the Alice.

Senior Arrente woman, Myra Hayes has told the court she can speak for Antoolya country, covered by a dreaming that stretches from Port Augusta in South Australia, up the Todd river through Alice Springs, to Bond Springs, north of the town, as well as an eagle dreaming to the east.
Mrs Hayes showed the court a sprig of bush she boils for use as medicine, saying the old people told her where to find it on her country.
he has also told the court where the soakages used to be in her traditional country, including one where a casino stands.
Mrs Hayes told the court she had painted this country for the judge, Justice Olney, with help from children she is teaching.
The Federal court will visit sites this morning, in the east of the town, significant to the eagle dreaming.
